title: Best AEOCKY Dehumidifier (2026): Models Ranked by Real DOE Pints
dek: Big numbers on the box, solid efficiency underneath — here's how to read an AEOCKY dehumidifier's real capacity before you buy.
description: The best AEOCKY dehumidifier for 2026, ranked on ENERGY STAR data: what the 80- and 140-pint labels really mean, who makes them, warranty and reviews.
intro: If you've shopped for an AEOCKY dehumidifier on Amazon, you've seen the headline: 80, 105, even 140 pints a day from a machine that weighs about 31 pounds. Those figures aren't fake, but they come from a very hot, very wet test condition (95°F and 95% humidity). Measured the way Midea, Frigidaire and GE rate their units — the DOE's 2019 test at 65°F and 60% humidity — the numbers shrink to roughly a third.

That doesn't make AEOCKY a bad brand. Look past the labels and several models carry ENERGY STAR's **Most Efficient** designation, and the compressor units come with a three-year warranty, which is longer than many rivals offer. The trick is comparing on the DOE number, not the marketing one.

Below we rank the AEOCKY lineup using ENERGY STAR's certified-product data, AEOCKY's manuals and warranty policy, and owner reviews — plus the models we'd skip and a cheaper alternative worth considering.
topPicksLead: For most basements, the **AEOCKY Leo-Lite3** is the AEOCKY to buy: a Most Efficient-rated chassis that ENERGY STAR lists at 44.94 pints a day, without paying extra for a pump you may not need.

products.name: AEOCKY Leo-Lite3 Dehumidifier (sold as 140-pint)
pros: ENERGY STAR rates it at 44.94 pints/day under the DOE test
Highly efficient at 2.21 liters per kWh
Same certified chassis as the pump-equipped Leo-003
cons: No pump — bucket or gravity hose only
Box label overstates capacity about threefold
products.whyWeLoveIt: The Leo-Lite3 is certified under the same ENERGY STAR basic model as AEOCKY's flagship pump unit, so you get the same capacity and efficiency while skipping the pump. If you have a floor drain or don't mind a bucket, that's the smartest way into the brand.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR lists it at 44.94 pints a day, 2.21 L/kWh and an estimated 438 kWh a year. That efficiency figure places the chassis among only nine of 273 portable listings in its 25–50-pint class that meet ENERGY STAR's Most Efficient criteria. In practice, it's a full-basement machine that sits a little below a true 50-pint unit on capacity but uses less electricity doing it. AEOCKY markets it as a standard ENERGY STAR model, so don't expect a Most Efficient badge on the box.

products.name: AEOCKY Leo-003 Dehumidifier with Pump (sold as 140-pint)
pros: Built-in pump with a 16.4-foot (5 m) hose included
Same 44.94-pint DOE rating as the Leo-Lite3
cons: Bucket is small relative to output
Rated watts and amps aren't published
products.whyWeLoveIt: If the unit has to sit below your nearest drain, the Leo-003 is the AEOCKY to pick. Its pump pushes condensate up and out, and the extra cost goes entirely to that pump rather than to a different machine.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR rates it identically to the Leo-Lite3: 44.94 pints a day at 2.21 L/kWh. AEOCKY includes a 5-meter hose and says the pump passed more than 10,000 reliability cycles. Owners note the bucket fills quickly if you don't use the pump or a hose. Because AEOCKY doesn't list wattage, use ENERGY STAR's 438 kWh-a-year estimate to gauge running cost. See every brand's self-draining options in our [dehumidifiers with a pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

products.name: AEOCKY Rhea-001 Dehumidifier (sold as 80-pint)
pros: Slim body for a living space
Listed at 44–53 dB across fan speeds
products.whyWeLoveIt: Size it like what it is — a 24.5-pint unit — and the Rhea-001 is a good one. It's efficient, relatively quiet and slim enough to sit in a bedroom, office or small finished basement.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR lists 24.50 pints a day at 1.86 L/kWh, and flags it Most Efficient. AEOCKY's spec sheet gives 44–53 dB across fan speeds. Ignore the listing's whole-house coverage claim; a 25-pint-class dehumidifier is a one-room machine. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) maps DOE pints to room sizes.
products.notes: If you buy through a marketplace, confirm the seller is AEOCKY or an authorized channel — the warranty only covers authorized purchases.

products.name: AEOCKY X1-Pro Desiccant Dehumidifier
pros: Zeolite desiccant rotor doesn't frost up
Compact for sheds, garages and RVs
cons: 340-watt heater uses more power per pint
products.whyWeLoveIt: Compressor dehumidifiers ice up as temperatures fall toward 40°F. The X1-Pro uses a heated desiccant wheel instead, so it keeps working in an unheated garage, shed or camper when a compressor would stall.
products.performance: AEOCKY quotes about 10 pints a day at 95°F and 90% humidity, and roughly 5 pints at 86°F and 80% — small-space capacity. Its 340-watt heater means running it nonstop uses about 8.2 kWh a day, so buy it for cold, not for savings. Compare it with Ivation and Eva-Dry models in our [desiccant dehumidifier](/best/best-desiccant-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.whyWeLoveIt: If you simply want a big-name 50-pint machine with a pump and an honest capacity label, this Midea is the benchmark every AEOCKY should be compared against: its 50 pints is the number you'd compare directly with other brands, no conversion needed.
products.performance: Midea rates it at 50 pints a day with ENERGY STAR certification and coverage up to 4,500 square feet, which puts it a little above the Leo-003's DOE-equivalent capacity. AEOCKY's advantages are the longer warranty, a slimmer body and the Leo line's strong efficiency figures; Midea's are the plain-language rating and wide availability. More Midea options are in our [best Midea dehumidifier](/best/best-midea-dehumidifier/) guide.

AEOCKY ENERGY STAR listings flagged Most Efficient
Limited warranty on AEOCKY's compressor models

blocks.text: The first number is the one to memorize. Divide any AEOCKY headline capacity by about 3.2 and you get a figure you can compare directly with other brands. An 80-pint AEOCKY competes with 22- to 25-pint Midea and Frigidaire units, not their 50-pint models.

We don't lab-test. We pulled every AEOCKY listing from ENERGY STAR's certified-dehumidifier dataset, which reports DOE capacity, efficiency (IEF, in liters per kWh), estimated annual energy and Most Efficient status. We then read AEOCKY's store pages, user manuals and warranty policy, checked the CPSC recall database, and looked for recurring themes in owner reviews.
We ranked on DOE capacity and efficiency first, then drainage, warranty and value relative to big-name alternatives.

sections.heading: What to look for in an AEOCKY dehumidifier

items.label: The DOE pint rating
items.text: Use ENERGY STAR's number, not the box claim. The 80-pint tier is about 24.5 DOE pints; the 140-pint tier is about 45.

items.label: The 80- or 140-pint tier
items.text: Those are the Most Efficient chassis. The 105-pint tier costs almost as much as the 140 and isn't.

items.label: A pump only if you need it
items.text: If there's a drain lower than the unit, a gravity hose does the same job as the Leo-003's pump.

items.label: An authorized seller
items.text: AEOCKY's warranty covers the original buyer from its own store, its Amazon storefront or another authorized channel.

items.label: The right room size
items.text: Ignore whole-house coverage claims and size by DOE pints. Our [whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) picks cover truly large homes.

sections.heading: Who makes AEOCKY dehumidifiers — and is AEOCKY a good brand?

blocks.text: AEOCKY doesn't name a manufacturer on its store, but ENERGY STAR requires one. Its listings are certified by **Invitop** — Zhuhai Invitop Technology, with one older model under sister company Guangdong Invitop — a China-based maker that also certifies dehumidifiers for brands such as Vellgoo, Deciuu and two Waykar models. Several are exact twins of AEOCKY units, sharing the same chassis and ratings.

So is it a good brand? The hardware is a solid, efficient mid-tier compressor design, and the three-year warranty beats Midea's one year. Where AEOCKY falls short is honesty on the box. Buy on the DOE number and you'll get a good machine; buy on the headline number and you'll likely undersize. We found no AEOCKY entries in the CPSC recall database.

AEOCKY publishes user manuals on its own store's product pages. Like most compressor dehumidifiers, its models let you set a target humidity, run continuously, and adjust fan speed; exact modes vary by model, so check the manual for yours. A good starting setting is 45–50%; our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) has seasonal targets.

Warranty-wise, compressor models get a three-year limited warranty, and the Leo-Lite manual adds five years on the compressor. The desiccant X1-Pro and thermoelectric VivaSilent get one year. Coverage excludes commercial, rental and shared use.

The **AEOCKY Leo-Lite3** is the best AEOCKY dehumidifier for most basements, with a Most Efficient-rated 44.94-pint chassis and a three-year warranty. Choose the **Leo-003** if you need a pump, and the **Rhea-001** for one room — just remember it's a 24.5-pint machine. If you'd rather skip the capacity math, the **Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump** is a plainly rated 50-pint alternative. See how AEOCKY stacks up against bigger names in our [best dehumidifier brands](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) ranking.

faqs.q: Is the AEOCKY 80-pint dehumidifier really 80 pints?
faqs.a: Only at 95°F and 95% humidity. Under the DOE test used by other major brands, ENERGY STAR lists the 80-pint Rhea-001 and Leo-001 at 24.50 pints a day. Divide any AEOCKY headline number by about 3.2 to compare it fairly.

faqs.q: Can an AEOCKY dehumidifier cover 4,500 sq ft?
faqs.a: Not in the way most shoppers expect. Coverage claims are based on the inflated box rating. Even the largest AEOCKY models rate about 45 DOE pints a day — basement or large-room capacity, not a whole 4,500-square-foot house in humid weather.

ENERGY STAR's dataset names Invitop — Zhuhai Invitop Technology and its sister company Guangdong Invitop — as the certifying manufacturer. The same Chinese manufacturer certifies near-identical units for several other Amazon brands.

Its hardware is efficient — several models carry ENERGY STAR's Most Efficient designation — and its three-year warranty is generous. The weak spot is inflated capacity labeling, so buy on the DOE rating.

faqs.q: What warranty do AEOCKY dehumidifiers have?
faqs.a: Three years on compressor models, with the Leo-Lite manual adding five years on the compressor itself. Desiccant and thermoelectric models get one year. The warranty only covers original buyers from authorized sellers.

faqs.q: What do AEOCKY dehumidifier reviews say?
faqs.a: Owners generally praise the efficiency and slim cabinets. Common complaints are small buckets relative to output, short included hoses on some models, and missing wattage figures on pump units.

faqs.q: Where can I find an AEOCKY dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: AEOCKY posts manuals on its own store's product pages. Search your exact model name, such as Leo-Lite3 or Rhea-001, since settings and drainage setup differ between models.
